findings.title: /api/auth 404 fallback is named but not actionable
findings.where: §4 (Decision — api/ functions), §11.1 (Reconciliation of api/ + custom outputDirectory), AC-5
findings.problem: The entire OAuth feature depends on repo-root api/*.js deploying as functions while outputDirectory is _site. The design validates this only via AC-5 [B], but the stated fallback is self-admittedly a no-op rewrite plus 'relocate them' — relocation is unspecified (to where, and how do redirect_uri/base_url/callback-URL, which hard-code /api/callback, change to match). An implementer hitting a 404 has only a direction, not a decided recovery.
findings.fix: Specify a complete fallback config instead of a direction: if AC-5 404s, add to vercel.json "functions": { "api/*.js": { "runtime": "@vercel/node@3.2.0" } } using a fully-qualified version (not a truncated major), which cures the zero-config miss without triggering 'Function Runtimes must have a valid version' and needs no function relocation or OAuth URL change.

findings.title: Date-ordering justification rests on a false Jekyll behavior for custom collections
findings.problem: The design repeatedly claims the YYYY-MM-DD- filename prefix alone guarantees Jekyll gives the document a real Time and thus the sort order. That is a _posts-only behavior; Jekyll does not derive 'date' from a custom-collection (_papers) filename. Ordering and %Y actually work only because the required front-matter 'date:' is a YAML date. The outcome holds today (date is REQUIRED), but the documented rule is wrong and could mislead a future hand-author into omitting date:, breaking sort and %Y.
findings.fix: Correct the justification: ordering/%Y come solely from the REQUIRED front-matter date: (unquoted YYYY-MM-DD cast to Time); the filename prefix is a readability/URL convention only and Jekyll does not derive date from a custom-collection filename. State that every paper (Decap or hand-authored) must carry date: in front matter; verify via seed paper and AC-6/AC-7.

findings.title: Home-page HTML comment nodes dropped by the includes
findings.problem: The real pages contain explanatory HTML comments that the includes/layouts omit. Rendering-irrelevant, but comments are not whitespace, so AC-2's 'matching the current hand-written home page' is slightly broader than delivered.
findings.fix: Add to §6's allowed-differences list: '(d) HTML comment nodes present in the current files may be dropped — they do not affect rendering.'

findings.title: Paper-body link underline is new styling vs existing links
findings.problem: Existing notebook links (.toc-item a, .back-link) use text-decoration: none; paper-body links will be underlined — a new visual treatment. Confined to .paper-body so NFR-2 holds, but worth calling out so it isn't mistaken for the no-restyle invariant leaking.
findings.fix: Note in §7.3/§7.4 that underlined paper-body links are a deliberate prose-convention choice confined to .paper-body and do not touch existing link selectors.

findings.title: .gitignore appended block mixes entries with wrapped prose comments
findings.problem: The block interleaves real ignore entries with multi-line prose (one comment is wrapped mid-word with a soft hyphen), risking a stray character on copy-paste and spreading the _site/ intent across §5.1/§4/§11.1.
findings.fix: Reduce the appended block to the four real entries (.jekyll-cache/, .sass-cache/, .bundle/, vendor/) plus a single short comment; keep the Alternative-B _site/ note in prose only.

findings.title: OAuth scope=repo broader than least-privilege
findings.problem: scope=repo grants full read/write to all of the user's repos to commit Markdown into one. Justified only as 'works whether or not the repo is private'. For a single public-repo CMS, public_repo is narrower.
findings.fix: Decide explicitly: use public_repo if benjaminmanoj/benmanoj is public (narrower), reserving repo for a future private repo; or if repo is already accepted, record the breadth tradeoff explicitly.

findings.title: Decap CDN URL and version range unverified
findings.problem: The @^3.0.0 range in the URL path and the dist/decap-cms.js filename are asserted from convention, not verified; a path-range resolves to latest 3.x and can drift. AC-8 checks config fields but not that the host page actually loads the bundle.
findings.fix: Pin a concrete known-good version (decap-cms@3.x.y) instead of a range in the URL and confirm the dist path during implementation; extend AC-8 to assert the host page loads the bundle.
